name: Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS Preview
access: Gemini API (Interactions API and generateContent; REST and SDKs)
Google Cloud Text-to-Speech API (model name gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview, in the global region; a separate prompt field and a text field)
Vertex AI API (generateContent; the global region)

voice.input_audio: none: the model takes text only. On the Gemini API, direction goes inside the text, as an optional prompt (Audio Profile, Scene, Director's Notes) and as square-bracket tags [g-archive-guide]. The Cloud Text-to-Speech API has a separate prompt field of up to 4,000 bytes and a text field of up to 4,000 bytes [g-cloud-tts]
voice.output_audio: Gemini API: headerless raw PCM (audio/l16, 24 kHz, 16-bit, mono) by default; Google's migration notes say 3.8 changed the unary default to WAV [g-tts-guide]. Cloud Text-to-Speech API: unary LINEAR16 (default), ALAW, MULAW, MP3, OGG_OPUS and PCM, and streaming PCM (default), ALAW, MULAW and OGG_OPUS; the Vertex AI API returns 16-bit 24 kHz PCM without a WAV header [g-cloud-tts]. All output carries a SynthID watermark [g-blog-31]
voice.voices: 30 prebuilt voices chosen in speech_config; no voice design and no voice replication [g-archive-guide] [g-tts-guide]
languages: 70+ languages by the launch post, with automatic detection of the input language; the archived guide lists them with BCP-47 codes [g-blog-31] [g-archive-guide]
voice.turn_detection: none: a synthesis model. A multi-speaker request names up to 2 speakers in the config and the transcript labels each line with a speaker name [g-archive-guide]
voice.interruption: Not a conversation model. Streaming has been available since 2026-06-17; the pages read describe no barge-in message [g-changelog] [g-archive-guide]
voice.latency: Google publishes no time-to-first-audio figure; it calls the model low latency. Artificial Analysis reports a median of 29.1 characters generated per second (throughput, not latency) [aa-g31] [g-model-31-page]
voice.session_limit: Input up to 8,192 tokens and output up to 16,384 tokens on the model page; the model card gives 16K text in and 32K tokens of audio out; the archived guide gave a session context limit of 32k tokens. The guide advises splitting transcripts that run longer than a few minutes [g-model-31-page] [g-card-31] [g-archive-guide]. On the Cloud Text-to-Speech API the text and prompt fields are at most 4,000 bytes each and 8,000 bytes together, and output past about 655 seconds is truncated [g-cloud-tts]

pricing_usd_per_mtok.notes: Per token, Gemini API Standard tier, paid plan [g-pricing]. The input field is the text rate and the output field is the audio rate. Batch costs half: US$0.50 in and US$10.00 out. Audio counts 25 tokens a second. The model page says caching is not supported. Google Cloud's price list shows the same US$1.00 and US$20.00 [g-cloud-pricing]. Artificial Analysis converts the price to US$18.3 per 1M characters [aa-pv].

benchmarks.name: Artificial Analysis Speech Arena Elo (provider voice leaderboard)
benchmarks.setting: blind pairwise listener votes on each provider's own voices; rank 13 of 93 (range 10 to 14), 3,706 votes, 7 voices; the model page gives 1208.55 and the leaderboard table gives 1209

benchmarks.name: Artificial Analysis text-to-speech median characters per second
benchmarks.setting: median generation speed in the benchmark run; read from the data on the model page

benchmarks.name: RW-Voice-EQ Bench, Acting / Role-Fit (human Likert mean)
benchmarks.setting: five-point Likert mean with a standard deviation of 0.04, default voice and settings; the highest of 31 configurations in the dimension. A paper by a speech vendor; the preview model was evaluated

benchmarks.name: RW-Voice-EQ Bench, Expressiveness (human Likert mean)
benchmarks.setting: five-point Likert mean with a standard deviation of 0.04; the highest of 31 configurations in the dimension. A paper by a speech vendor
